title: Plier-decap a serum bottle: squeeze and twist the crimp seal off, then ease the grip so the seal drops into the beaker
instruction: Remove the aluminum crimp seal from the serum bottle with the plier decapper, drop the seal in the waste beaker and put the decapper down on the counter. Touch the seal only with the decapper's jaws, and move both hands away at the end.
context: Chromatography and headspace-GC labs, pharma QC and anaerobic-culture labs close vials and serum bottles with 20 mm aluminum crimp seals and remove them with a hand decapper to re-sample, empty or recycle the glass. WHEATON's guide for its 224373 plier decapper: "secure the seal between the jaws, squeeze the handles and twist the seal". O*NET 19-4031.00 Chemical Technicians, core task: "Set up and conduct chemical experiments, tests, and analyses, using techniques such as chromatography ..."
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left); heights above the counter. Lab preparation counter (the table) with a white reagent shelf at the back (800 wide, 420 tall, front at x 495). WHEATON 223747 100 mL clear glass serum bottle (52 diameter, 95 tall with its seal; 110 g, an estimate), empty, standing at x 290, y 50, closed with a grey W224100-405 stopper under a WHEATON 224178-01 20 mm open-top aluminum seal crimped over the 20 mm finish (seal 21.5 outside, 7.6 tall, 13 mm centre hole, about 1 g: estimates). WHEATON 224373 plier decapper (steel, grey plastic-coated handles; 157 long, 160 g, estimates) lying flat on its handles, jaws pointing +y, rivet at x 250, y -120, its jaws open 0.55 rad from closed on the seal (jaw tips 32 apart; fixture/dimensions.svg). PYREX 1000-250 250 mL low-form glass beaker (68 outside x 90; 110 g, an estimate), empty, at x 370, y -45. Lot B: bottle at x 270, y 80 and beaker at x 365, y -15; the plier as in lot A. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A. Lower-cost real trial (about US$450, priced in README): the same plier decapper; 100 mL serum bottles with the same 20 mm finish in a pack of 36 (51.7 x 94.5 mm, reused; only the seal is used up); 20 mm aluminum seals and grey butyl stoppers in packs of 100; a generic 20 mm hand crimper in place of the E-Z Crimper; and any 250 mL low-form beaker.
scoring: Read from the overhead video and a side camera level with the seal, stepped frame by frame, close photos of the bottle neck against a 1 mm rule, and a 10x loupe. Score 0 for the whole trial if, at any moment, a robot finger touches the aluminum seal (simulation: over 0.5 N), the plier chips or cracks the glass (loupe; simulation: over 20 N of plier-on-glass contact), or the bottle or beaker falls over (tilts past 45 degrees). Every score needs, for the last 1 s, the bottle standing (tilted 10 degrees or less, base within 3 mm of the counter) and the bottle, seal, beaker and plier still. 1.0: the seal lies inside the waste beaker below its rim, the plier lies on the counter (lowest point within 4 mm of it, tilted 15 degrees or less), and both hands have been at least 30 mm from all four for 1 s. 0.75: seal in the beaker; the plier not put down or the hands not clear. 0.5: the seal off the bottle, no part of it within 10 mm of the glass or stopper (simulation: an 11.5 mm sphere round its centre), but not in the beaker. 0.25: the crimp is torn (the seal is loose and turns on the neck; simulation: it has turned 90 degrees in all, in steps of 0.5 degree or more, while both jaws pressed it with 10 N or more) but the seal is still on or near the bottle. 0 otherwise. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged.
run_limit: 2,400 steps (120 s at 20 Hz) per trial; two trials (lots A and B)
reset_notes: Each trial uses up one seal. 1. Take an empty WHEATON 223747 bottle, check the finish under a 10x loupe and reject any chip; fit a new W224100-405 stopper and crimp a new 224178-01 seal with a 20 mm hand crimper (WHEATON W225303 E-Z Crimper) at its maker's setting; reject a seal that turns by hand. 2. Empty the waste beaker. 3. Stand the bottle and the beaker on their lot's tape outlines; lay the plier flat on its outline with its jaws open 0.55 rad from closed on the seal (jaw tips 32 mm apart; check against the 1:1 drawing in fixture/dimensions.svg). 4. Both arms at their start pose. Recycle the torn seal.
fidelity: True size from maker data: bottle 52 x 95 mm, 20 mm finish; beaker 68 x 90 mm. Plier, seal and stopper sizes and masses are estimates, from boxes and cylinders; the seal collides as a solid 21.5 mm cylinder. Declared crimp: the seal stays on the finish until turned 90 degrees in all while both jaws press it with 10 N or more, then is a loose 1 g part; no tearing, and no twisting load reaches the bottle. Rivet holds 0.48 N m, then slips; eases back up to 0.08 rad. Chipping: a 20 N contact rule.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (mean of lots A and B, 0 in each; both ran to the 2,400-step limit without refusing; the right hand moved over the plier but never gripped the seal); demo: 1.0 in each of lots A and B (crimp torn at about 18 s, full score at about 39 s)
